raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #60348. `Internlm2ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` rebuilt each argument delta from
the re-serialized partial parse, so characters went missing and the concatenated deltas were not the
completed arguments. It now streams slices of the raw argument text, tracking how much has been sent.

## Claims

- The concatenated argument deltas reconstruct the complete arguments JSON for every chunk boundary
  I tried, instead of losing characters such as `{"location": "Beijing, "days": 3`.
- `"parameters": {}` now streams `{}` rather than nothing.
- Braces inside a string value no longer confuse the end of the arguments object.

## Validation

New parametrized test `test_streaming_arguments_survive_every_chunk_boundary` in
`tests/tool_parsers/test_internlm2_tool_parser.py`, cutting the body at 1, 3, 6 and 12 characters
because what gets lost depends on where the boundary lands, asserting the concatenation is exactly
`{"city": "Beijing", "days": 3}`.

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_internlm2_tool_parser.py
```

Driving the parser over 5 argument bodies (two keys, three keys, three-level nesting, a `}` inside a
string value, and `{}`) against 8 chunkings each: 40 of 40 combinations lose characters before this
change, 0 of 40 after. A second sweep over escaped strings (embedded quote, backslash, newline,
emoji, braces), all JSON value types and a pretty-printed multi-line body reconstructs the arguments
at every chunking, the existing `test_streaming_arguments_in_single_delta` scenario is unchanged, and
the five malformed inputs from the shared test config still return without raising when split
mid-string.

What the deltas now carry is the model's own argument text, so it is byte-identical to the
non-streaming `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` only when the model emits that style; for a
compact or pretty-printed body the concatenation is JSON-equivalent rather than byte-equal. That is
the contract the Hermes parser already ships.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on `vllm/tool_parsers/internlm2_tool_parser.py`.

The shared `ToolParserTests` streaming cases for this parser stay `xfail`: they feed
`<|action_start|>` and `<|plugin|>` as separate token deltas and the marker check in this parser does
not join them. That is a different defect and this change does not touch it.

Model evaluation: not applicable. This only changes how already-decoded tool-call arguments are cut
into streaming deltas in the API layer — no weights, sampling, kernels or scheduling, so identical
generated text gives identical results.

## Details

The `cur_arguments and prev_arguments` branch computed deltas with `extract_intermediate_diff` over
`json.dumps` of two successive partial parses, and the `cur_arguments and not prev_arguments` branch
located the delta inside a re-serialized parse. Both rest on the serialized partial parse growing by
append, and it does not: `partial_json_parser` closes the object optimistically, so the `"` and `}`
it invents for one parse are gone from the next. Once a delta containing an invented character has
been sent, the stream is no longer a prefix of the finished arguments, so the missing characters
cannot be recovered and `get_remaining_unstreamed_args` cannot flush them either. On top of that,
the first parse that carries arguments is the same call that sends the function name, so
`prev_arguments` becomes non-`None` before anything has been streamed and the leading
`{"location": "Beijing"` is simply skipped.

The raw argument text, by contrast, only ever grows by append, so a character count into it is a
valid resume point. `get_raw_arguments` returns the raw object text as far as it has arrived, using a
small left-to-right scan that tracks string literals and escapes so a brace inside a value is not
read as the closing brace. Because the scan stops at the matching brace, what it returns for a prefix
of the action is always a prefix of what it returns for the whole, which is what makes the slice
safe. The streaming branch then sends `raw[len(already_streamed):]` and records the new length. The
partial parse is still used for the function name and for `prev_tool_call_arr`, which serving code
reads.

`jamba_tool_parser.py` has the same `extract_intermediate_diff` pattern. I kept this PR to the parser
the issue reports so the change stays reviewable; happy to do Jamba in a follow-up.

Not a duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "60348 in:body"` is empty. Of the open PRs on this
file, #57504 buffers the partial opening marker, #58346 fixes a `ValueError` on a second action
block, #50078 and #44140 handle malformed output, and #47968 returns early for unlisted tool names —
none of them changes how argument deltas are computed. #50461 does touch the same branch, and its
description sets out the loss it addresses and the class of argument bodies it leaves open; #60348 is
in that remaining class, and this PR closes it by not deriving deltas from the serialized parse at
all rather than by reconciling one afterwards.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -162,3 +162,61 @@ def test_streaming_arguments_in_single_delta(default_tokenizer: TokenizerLike) -
                 streamed += arguments
 
     assert json.loads(streamed) == {"city": "Dallas", "state": "TX"}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "chunk_size",
+    [1, 3, 6, 12],
+    ids=["1_char_deltas", "3_char_deltas", "6_char_deltas", "12_char_deltas"],
+)
+def test_streaming_arguments_survive_every_chunk_boundary(
+    default_tokenizer: TokenizerLike, chunk_size: int
+) -> None:
+    """Streamed argument deltas must concatenate to the completed arguments.
+
+    Deltas rebuilt from the re-serialized partial parse used to drop characters:
+    partial_json_parser closes the object optimistically, so the quote it invents
+    for one parse is gone from the next and the stream stops being a prefix of the
+    finished arguments. The body is cut at several sizes because the loss depends
+    on where the boundary falls.
+    """
+    tokenizer_vocab = default_tokenizer.get_vocab()
+    default_tokenizer.get_vocab = MagicMock()
+    tokenizer_vocab.update(
+        {
+            "<|action_start|>": 92540,
+            "<|plugin|>": 92541,
+            "<|action_end|>": 92542,
+        }
+    )
+    default_tokenizer.get_vocab.return_value = tokenizer_vocab
+    parser = Internlm2ToolParser(default_tokenizer)
+
+    body = '{"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Beijing", "days": 3}}'
+    deltas = (
+        ["<|action_start|><|plugin|>"]
+        + [body[i : i + chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(body), chunk_size)]
+        + ["<|action_end|>"]
+    )
+
+    streamed = ""
+    current_text = ""
+    for delta_text in deltas:
+        previous_text = current_text
+        current_text += delta_text
+        delta_message = parser.extract_tool_calls_streaming(
+            previous_text=previous_text,
+            current_text=current_text,
+            delta_text=delta_text,
+            previous_token_ids=[],
+            current_token_ids=[],
+            delta_token_ids=[],
+            request=None,
+        )
+        if delta_message and delta_message.tool_calls:
+            arguments = delta_message.tool_calls[0].function.arguments
+            if arguments:
+                streamed += arguments
+
+    assert json.loads(streamed) == {"city": "Beijing", "days": 3}
+    assert streamed == '{"city": "Beijing", "days": 3}'

@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@
 from collections.abc import Sequence
 
 import partial_json_parser
+import regex as re
 from partial_json_parser.core.options import Allow
 
 from vllm.entrypoints.chat_utils import make_tool_call_id
@@ -26,7 +27,6 @@
     Tool,
     ToolParser,
 )
-from vllm.tool_parsers.utils import extract_intermediate_diff, is_complete_json
 
 logger = init_logger(__name__)
 
@@ -47,6 +47,40 @@ def adjust_request(
             request.skip_special_tokens = False
         return request
 
+    def get_raw_arguments(self, action: str) -> str | None:
+        """Raw text of the arguments object in ``action``, as far as it has arrived.
+
+        The scan tracks string literals and escapes, so a brace inside a string
+        value is not read as the end of the object. It runs left to right and
+        stops at the matching close brace, so what it returns for a prefix of
+        ``action`` is always a prefix of what it returns for the whole of it,
+        which is what makes streaming by character count safe.
+        """
+        match = re.search(r'"(?:parameters|arguments)"\s*:\s*(?=\{)', action)
+        if match is None:
+            return None
+        text = action[match.end() :]
+        depth = 0
+        in_string = False
+        escaped = False
+        for index, char in enumerate(text):
+            if in_string:
+                if escaped:
+                    escaped = False
+                elif char == "\\":
+                    escaped = True
+                elif char == '"':
+                    in_string = False
+            elif char == '"':
+                in_string = True
+            elif char == "{":
+                depth += 1
+            elif char == "}":
+                depth -= 1
+                if depth == 0:
+                    return text[: index + 1]
+        return text
+
     def get_arguments(self, obj):
         if "parameters" in obj:
             return obj.get("parameters")
@@ -128,55 +162,22 @@ def extract_tool_calls_streaming(
             # now we know we're on the same tool call and we're streaming
             # arguments
             else:
-                prev_arguments = self.get_arguments(
-                    self.prev_tool_call_arr[self.current_tool_id]
+                # Stream slices of the raw argument text, tracking how much of it
+                # has already been sent. Deltas rebuilt from the re-serialized
+                # partial parse cannot be trusted: partial_json_parser closes the
+                # object optimistically, so a quote or brace it invented for one
+                # parse is absent from the next, and once a delta containing one
+                # has gone out the stream is no longer a prefix of the finished
+                # arguments and the missing characters can never be sent.
+                raw_arguments = self.get_raw_arguments(action)
+                streamed = self.streamed_args_for_tool[self.current_tool_id]
+
+                argument_diff = (
+                    raw_arguments[len(streamed) :] if raw_arguments is not None else ""
                 )
-                cur_arguments = self.get_arguments(tool_call_arr)
-
-                # not arguments generated
-                if not cur_arguments and not prev_arguments:
-                    delta = None
-                # will never happen
-                elif not cur_arguments and prev_arguments:
-                    logger.error(
-                        "INVARIANT - impossible to have arguments reset mid-arguments"
-                    )
+                if not argument_diff:
                     delta = None
-                # first time to get parameters
-                elif cur_arguments and not prev_arguments:
-                    cur_arguments_json = json.dumps(cur_arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
-
-                    match_start = cur_arguments_json.find(delta_text)
-                    if match_start != -1:
-                        arguments_delta = cur_arguments_json[
-                            : match_start + len(delta_text)
-                        ]
-                    elif is_complete_json(parsable_arr):
-                        # Complete in this delta: send whole, don't drop.
-                        arguments_delta = cur_arguments_json
-                    else:
-                        # Still partial: wait for more text.
-                        return None
-                    delta = DeltaMessage(
-                        tool_calls=[
-                            DeltaToolCall(
-                                index=self.current_tool_id,
-                                function=DeltaFunctionCall(
-                                    arguments=arguments_delta
-                                ).model_dump(exclude_none=True),
-                            )
-                        ]
-                    )
-                    self.streamed_args_for_tool[self.current_tool_id] += arguments_delta
-                # both prev and cur parameters, send the increase parameters
-                elif cur_arguments and prev_arguments:
-                    cur_args_json = json.dumps(cur_arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
-                    prev_args_json = json.dumps(prev_arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
-
-                    argument_diff = extract_intermediate_diff(
-                        cur_args_json, prev_args_json
-                    )
-
+                else:
                     delta = DeltaMessage(
                         tool_calls=[
                             DeltaToolCall(
@@ -187,7 +188,7 @@ def extract_tool_calls_streaming(
                             )
                         ]
                     )
-                    self.streamed_args_for_tool[self.current_tool_id] += argument_diff
+                    self.streamed_args_for_tool[self.current_tool_id] = raw_arguments
 
             # check to see if the name is defined and has been sent. if so,
             # stream the name - otherwise keep waiting
